title.narrative: Critical Multisectoral Emergency Assistance for Unregistered South Sudanese Refugees

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtSince February 2025, Gambella Region has hosted over 53,000 new refugees from South Sudan following increased fighting in the Jonglei and Upper Nile states of South Sudan. Most newly arrived refugees are settling temporarily in Wantawo and Makuey woredas in readiness for transition to the formal UNHCR-managed collective site in Luok Dong. The influx of new refugees, in combination with existing refugee populations, internal displacement, and floods, has caused significant strains on already limited resources, leaving refugees and host communities in need of essential services. ltbrgtThis project is designed in response to the EHF’s 2025 third reserve allocation call and will contribute to addressing the critical unmet needs of 37,600 (22,560 female) newly arrived and unregistered refugees from South Sudan and host communities. It will stabilize conditions for refugees to facilitate their eventual transfer to Luok Dong collective site. ltbrgtThe project is co-designed and implemented by ZOA (consortium lead and ES/NFI, WASH, Gender, and Peace sector specialist), Ethiopian Kale Hiwot Church Humanitarian Aid and Development Commission (EKHC-HADC) (local NGO, sub-applicant and nutrition and protection sector specialist), and Gambella People with Disabilities Federation (GPDF) (CBO and disability experts). It follows a complementary approach that leverages the expertise, resources, and local experience of partners, community, and government structures. During the project cycle, ZOA and EKHC-HADC will follow a common approach of joint planning, implementation, and monitoring, targeting the same people, at the same time, in the same place, based on common objectives and shared analysis of needs and priorities. The project delivers an integrated programme of activities increasing access to clean water, latrines, handwashing facilities, shelter, MHPSS, cholera, and nutrition services. Through the provision of equipment and training/coaching programmes, it improves the skills and knowledge of government and community workers, for example, monitoring water quality, child protection, and GBV case management. ZOA is also committed to strengthening the management and operational capacities of EKHC-HADC and GPDF, based on a joint assessment. Through community campaigns, this project aims to change behaviors relating to hygiene and sanitation, nutrition, and raise awareness of children’s rights and the community members' role in protection/GBV prevention and response, and conflict resolution. The project places protection at its core, ensures meaningful engagement of communities and stakeholders throughout design and implementation, and ensures access to safe, dignified, and inclusive services for vulnerable groups. Context-appropriate Complaint, Feedback, and Response Mechanisms (CFRM) will be established to amplify voices, address concerns, and improve accountability. To prevent duplication of resources/efforts and maximize the project impact, ZOA and EKHC-HADC will coordinate with humanitarian partners (i.e., IRC, SCI, Plan, DCA, Nexus, etc) who are active in the humanitarian response across the target woredas. The project will build on ZOA’s ongoing ECHO-RRM, EHF, and privately funded lifesaving responses for refugees and host communities in the target woredas. It complements EKHC-HADC ’s interventions with flood-affected families, vulnerable children, and HIV affected families within Gambella. ltbrgt ltbrgtlt/pgt
